## Result

- Skill: code-review.
- Status: completed.
- Review status: approved.
- Review ID: code-review-m2.
- Milestone: m2, coherent unified authoring and bounded ownership cutover.
- Exact diff: 9b36473e..f51445a4, including38e2fdc2 and final committed resource removals.
- Material findings / required review-resolution: none.
- Milestone closeout: this review supports Route closing M2 against these exact subjects; reviewer does not change work state.
- Remaining implementation milestones: none after Route confirms M2 and required evidence disposition.
- Next stage: fresh independent whole-change Code Review, then distinct final Verify.
- Final closeout / Verify readiness: not established by milestone approval.
- Recording: targeted v2 review.record, with present engineering subjects and explicit absence reads for removed files. The review subject schema requires concrete SHA-256 identities; removed paths remain in the exact inspected basis and committed deletion diff.

## Actual implementation judgment

The integration selects managed authoring replacement only when old entries exist, exact descriptor roots have one matching lock owner, no competing design exists and recorded tree/state checks pass. The initial basis precedes archive acquisition; the private transaction rechecks that original basis before publication. Archive trust/structure and retired-entry rejection precede writes. Ordinary installation, state-implicated ambiguity, local modifications/additions/predeletion, aliases and mixed owners do not gain a drift override. Both OpenCode roots are selected. Shared-state updates retain unrelated target entries and their drift checks. The synchronous public caller invokes the previously reviewed pinned-parent/no-clobber transaction without asynchronous interleaving inside its cwd/umask operation.

The helper retains original/private detached bytes, uses basename-only source and destination detachment within a pinned parent, no-clobber file publication and exclusive directory creation, and rechecks captured root/ancestor authority. Recovery evidence is private implementation data, not a public runtime record schema or semantic readiness service. Pending recovery accepts only a complete original or candidate snapshot; partial or independent changes block retry. Settlement accepts only the exact private value, rejects unknown values and symlinks, and occurs after coherent-basis inspection. A caught failure restores the original or reports retained paths and incomplete recovery; process interruption requires explicitly authorized operator restoration. The guide requires external complete backup and preservation/reconciliation of independent shared-state changes, and does not instruct managed users to pre-delete roots or reset hashes. Root/ancestor and late-descriptor protections from M1 remain exercised after the M2 additions.

The normal public author is design. Both retired package directories and their OpenCode aliases are absent in final committed source and archives. Common instructions reconcile behavior, technical choices, rationale and acceptance, with conditional depth for shared composition, examples, technical reasoning and retained feature/architecture/ADR amendments. Distinct Proposal, independent Design Review, Delivery, Code Review, Test policy and Verify ownership remain. The exact affected model/example/legacy handoff replaces the tuple; unknown/missing authority and package guidance have distinct stops. Scenario parsing, cross-record invariants and applicability after an example-only revision remain different obligations. The completed MW-01 walkthrough provides independently generated concrete outputs under all three installed resource sets, not only phrase-presence checks or an asserted target-agent transcript.

## First-pass checklist

| Item | Judgment and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Spec alignment | Pass: DES-SR01–20, System composition and TNI-DES01–06 map to one author, scoped ownership transfer, safe explicit upgrade and bounded migration. Current Design r6/Delivery r3 supply exact authority. |
| Test coverage | Pass: required helper/public, all-target, alias, state-implicated/unmanaged, interruption, failed rollback, concurrent-state and idempotence proof is present; full suites supplement direct MW01–03 outcomes. |
| Edge cases | Pass: tests distinguish missing/modified/extra/symlink/mixed bases, caught/process failures, restored retry, unrelated targets, before-final-call competing writes and original ancestor replacement. |
| Error handling | Pass: unsafe original/candidate or recovery evidence rejects; dry run neither reads archive contents nor writes; incomplete recovery retains evidence and does not accept a partial installation as current. |
| Architecture boundaries | Pass: shared policy/coordination/storage roles remain distinct; installer support remains private beneath retained installation owner; system view references component ownership without copying contracts. |
| Compatibility | Pass: current invocations change coherently; historical protocol/artifact/placement identities and archived decisions remain; unsupported old candidates reject without rewriting historical releases. |
| Security/privacy | Pass: explicit replacement scope, archive trust, path/root authority and no-clobber publication preserved; no external service, credentials, customer installation or broad force bypass introduced. |
| Derived currency | Pass for exact local candidate: measured current metadata and release-index digest match generated archives; three clean installs/resource closures pass. Historical release metadata is unchanged; publication not claimed. |
| Unrelated changes | Pass: directly required consumers/selectors/tests and current metadata only; user docs/design.zip preserved. Additional five source removals are committed, not merely absent locally. |
| Validation evidence | Pass for milestone scope: actual commands/results below and MW assessment are current for exercised behavior. Original failed baseline evidence remains historical/limited, not rewritten as passing. |

## Retirement enforcement and test maintenance

Independent MW-02 and Design r6 already traced numbered and unnumbered method obligations, decisions, selected mixed-System sections and three owned follow-up families. Those relied-on source identities remain current. The additional location compatibility notice retains historical metadata without recreating public authors. ADR bytes and historical review meaning remain preserved.

The new validator disposition is derived enforcement of the approved exact two-source retirement. It recognizes only the two named paths, verifies complete preserved source-plus-notice hashes and contained regular replacement owner files, and rejects changed/missing historical bytes, notices, partners or owners. No arbitrary Historical heading, unknown marker, path pattern or grandfathering rewrite bypasses validation. Other new/current feature format checks remain. The focused regressions prove preservation success and unknown/changed/missing negatives. This is structural preservation, not semantic approval of a replacement owner or arbitrary archive service.

Test changes replace obsolete author-path/literal assertions with the new resource and retained-method contract, preserve package/escape/unknown-value and independent-review protections, and retain historical measurement arithmetic without pretending a frozen old report measures the revised current skill. Source deletion routing omits prose audit only for proven deletions while retaining skill and package checks; unknown missing paths do not gain that treatment. No test removal is justified merely by absence from representative scenarios.

## Actual validation and evidence applicability

Reviewer independently ran:

- node --test packages/rigorloop/test/managed-authoring-replacement.test.js:38 passed.
- node --test --test-name-pattern 'DES ' packages/rigorloop/test/cli.test.js:16 passed.
- python scripts/test-boundary-first-validation.py RetiredMethodSourceTests:3 passed.

Inspected author-owned logs/evidence report454 Node,355 skill-validator,156 selector,87 boundary,158 adapter-distribution,7 skill-build and7 npm-publication tests passing, alongside projection, prose/readability, schema/lifecycle and current candidate validation. The adapter-suite historical negative-fixture Gate C messages occur after the successful suite and are not a claimed current release pass. Source tests are not substituted for the actual archive/installed/public execution proof.

Current candidate archive SHA-256:

- Codex:e72b5adb11ce124613cdcfbcfa2fbeb6e8b69a33b1db732f93a44840b30f8167.
- Claude:8fd30c8cc7db31fba773f80d806386fd0e15ce3b3cf37d6bf400a60a801b7139.
- OpenCode:a84612ab469877b771f3de454a1a13dacc301a344ab546f3dce00e33d0e7b270.

Fresh archive hashing matches MW-01 and MW-03 and measured metadata. MW-01 and MW-02 exact relied source sets have no drift. MW-03 raw subprocess transcript shows ordinary exit2, authorized success, process exit97, partial retry exit2, restored success and idempotent success against the same actual candidate and preserved old Codex neighbor. Its stored cli.test.js identity precedes three additional tests; its exercised CLI/helper/guide/metadata remain byte-identical. I affirm retained applicability of that bounded execution after inspecting the added-only tests and current full evidence; I do not retarget or rewrite its old execution subject. New public tests provide current complementary proof.

The earlier two architecture-method BFR failures remain recorded historical observations; current selected validation now applies the narrowly reviewed preservation check and passes. Thirteen unchanged historical installer prose errors remain failed baseline debt under the exact unchanged-body comparison and plan limit. No claim of universal prose success, blanket waiver, uncontrolled power-loss proof, target-agent correctness, public release or customer adoption is made. Final whole-change review and Verify must assess their own current basis and closeout obligations.

## Independence and handoff

Concrete independent nonauthor /root/independent_design_review. Primary-agent authored all production implementation and engineering text. Reviewer authored only synthetic customer walkthrough fixtures and independent evidence/reviews, and independently inspected final M2 diff, callers, tests, candidate archives and migration basis. Prior M1/Design/Delivery reviews inform bounded reliance; they do not substitute for this M2 decision.

Return this exact M2 judgment to Route. No routing, work, engineering or upstream-review mutation by this assessor.
